title: Language declaration and document direction
learningObjectives: Explain language declaration and document direction and apply accurate document metadata or print structure.

understand.concept: The lang attribute identifies the language of an element's text. The dir attribute sets text direction using ltr, rtl, or auto. A document should declare its primary language on the html element and mark language changes on specific passages where needed.
understand.whyItMatters: Language and direction help browsers, assistive technologies, search systems, and text layout behave appropriately. Do not use CSS text alignment as a substitute for correct direction semantics.
understand.analogy: lang tells tools which language is being spoken; dir tells them the direction in which the text flows.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser metadata and search/social platform processing are governed by their respective specifications and policies.

explain.narrative: The document declares English left-to-right text and a separate Arabic passage with right-to-left direction.

practise.guidedTask: Create a multilingual snippet with English and Telugu text, then add an RTL example. Explain why lang and dir are separate attributes.
practise.independentTask: Prepare metadata or print styles for a sample course page. Verify paths, content accuracy, language declarations, and the print result.
hints: Use absolute URLs where metadata requires them.
Do not invent structured data claims.
Keep the visible page consistent with metadata.

questions.prompt: What is the most important rule for page metadata?
options: It must accurately describe the actual page
It should contain as many keywords as possible
